Fixed in 1a204ed02d91a436b8111579a97bdf0efd7cd1ae. I had narrowed workflow-wide controls together with the decide permission block. Run expressions, multiline run blocks, event values outside the decide environment, and inline `gh` now scan `$wf`. Job-specific permission and concurrency checks remain on `$decide_wf`.

I ran the actual test against five temporary workflow mutations: apply and report run expressions, a report run block, a report event environment value, and inline `gh` in report. Before the fix all five incorrectly exited 0. After it all five exit 1 at the intended guard. No unsafe workflow was committed.

The normal decide, apply, report, app-token and protection suites pass. The CLI suite passes 69 cases, including the added bare-answer newline/code-block assertion. Shellcheck and actionlint are clean.

Read-only investigation confirms a blocking mint-authority issue, with an important correction to the example. The bounded repair is tracked in [#474](https://github.com/kitimark/mitos/issues/474).

GitHub's runner [merges declared input defaults](https://github.com/actions/runner/blob/7afce9edc81e4138ed1eaa673a3c10c811faa092/src/Runner.Worker/ActionRunner.cs#L206) and then [exports INPUT_*](https://github.com/actions/runner/blob/7afce9edc81e4138ed1eaa673a3c10c811faa092/src/Runner.Worker/Handlers/Handler.cs#L175) after the inherited environment. The literal INPUT_OWNER, INPUT_SKIP-TOKEN-REVOKE and declared hyphenated permission keys in the example are overwritten; those values did not change owner or revocation in the offline controls.

The [pinned v1.12.0 bundle](https://github.com/actions/create-github-app-token/blob/d72941d797fd3113feb6b93fd0dec494b13a2547/dist/main.cjs#L42531) instead enumerates the undeclared INPUT_PERMISSION_ underscore prefix. A new trusted mint workflow can pass the current native bundle check with canonical permission-contents:read plus either INPUT_PERMISSION_ADMINISTRATION in env or permission_administration in with. Executing the exact pinned bundle offline with request/auth dependencies stubbed reached actual installation-auth options containing administration:write. No token endpoint was contacted. The three existing finite production workflow contracts reject these extra YAML fields; new generic mint admission does not.

The pin also ignores ordinary canonical hyphenated permission inputs, leaving permissions undefined at baseline. Accordingly, this is a failure to enforce the promised explicit limits; it is not evidence of escalation beyond the installation's grant ceiling or beyond the already unnarrowed baseline.

Static inspection identifies actions/create-github-app-token@64ab729a6294000f5aa4a4bc0b73d1f32bc45510 (stable v3.3.0, node24) as the preferred candidate: its verified bundle uses the correct hyphenated collector in the actual entrypoint. Existing app-id/private-key inputs remain compatible; its proxy requirements must be checked. The Node20 v2.2.2 fallback already passed offline actual-bundle controls for all three intended permission maps. The chosen new pin still requires those runtime controls during repair validation. The proposed bounded repair pairs that pin change with a closed inventory of the three already reviewed finite mint contracts, rejecting additional generic mint workflows rather than trying to prove arbitrary shell/environment behavior by text matching. The same-major v1 tag still points to the defective pin.

The finding remains open and PR #336 stays blocked. The separately scoped repair will be handled by a fresh owner under the user’s standing request; that is root judgment, not a new user ruling. This is a concrete proposal, not an implemented fix. The separate helper-deduplication suggestion is minor follow-up. No source, token, key or merge change has been made for this diagnosis.

The current custom pre-merge assessment's new claim about exit status is incorrect. The command is `jq -ce`, so it includes `--exit-status` (`-e`). When `select` produces no result, that option returns status 4. A bounded execution of the exact filter with jq 1.7 gives 100 answers → status 0/nonempty output; 101 answers → status 4/empty output. The failed assignment reaches `|| return 1` before any GITHUB_OUTPUT write.

More directly, [current-head CI 44191970257](https://github.com/kitimark/mitos/actions/runs/44191970257/job/134423429921) passes both `answers-at-the-count-cap-are-handed-on` and `answers-over-the-count-cap-are-refused`. The [actual script controls](https://github.com/kitimark/mitos/blob/5c6fc5f82dea7cf0a0ff17589a5eaea0191034af/.github/scripts/land-decide.test.sh#L369) use a valid merge plan and reads, stay below the byte cap, and require exit 1 with no outputs for 101. No source change is needed for this static false positive; the intended refusal already executes and passes.
